references_named: Dutch vanitas still life (Harmen Steenwyck, Pieter Claesz)
Battery Status API and its removal for fingerprinting
rationale: A textbook P1 piece: the flame literally is navigator.getBattery().level — the mechanism enacts the vanitas rather than illustrating it, and removing the API call removes the concept. Double-coding is unusually crisp: the surface gag (candle that mirrors your phone's charge) carries a sharper literate reading in which the privacy ethic the practice already lives by has, on Firefox/Safari, denied the vanitas its own memento mori — the one API honest enough to tell you you're dying was killed for being too good at watching you. Restraint is exemplary: the unsupported state is attested, not explained; the Ecclesiastes quote sets the register; the footer labels the medium as 'the charge remaining in your device.'
reservations: The piece leans on a hardware API that Chromium is also reportedly deprecating in some contexts (the WebKit/Blink Battery API story has shifted over the years); a note attesting current support would harden the work. The reference to Perfect Lovers (Reset) is honestly handled but the two works will inevitably be read as a pair — the candidate may want to lean into that pairing more explicitly rather than only distinguishing itself.
revision_suggestion: Consider a one-line note in the label or footer about the current cross-browser state of the Battery Status API (and any planned deprecation) so the 'withheld' branch remains legible as the web platform moves; this also lets the work remain itself if the API disappears entirely, by shifting the argument from 'denied by the privacy ethic' to 'lost to the platform.'
